title: A simple non-absolutely-simple algebra is R-universal exactly when it is the restriction of scalars of a strongly inner algebra over an imaginary quadratic extension
author: Dave Witte Morris
work: A Cohomological Proof that Real Representations of Semisimple Lie Algebras Have Q-Forms
source_version: Official SIGMA 11 (2015) article 034, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2015.034; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the criterion for a simple algebra that is not absolutely simple (author prop at source lines 849-854): R-universality holds exactly when the algebra is the restriction of scalars of a strongly inner absolutely simple algebra over an imaginary quadratic extension. The proof (source lines 856-880) first forces the extension to be imaginary quadratic using the author's lemma on the minimal inner extension, and then compares the beta invariants of a weight and its restriction of scalars to show that the vanishing condition transfers in both directions (proof lines 859-879). The invariant comparison across the restriction of scalars is the step with content. H2.
